newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coalition, SPD start last-chance tax talks.
newsitem.headline: German coalition, SPD start last-chance tax talks.

text.p: Leaders of Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) arrived on Tuesday at the chancellery for tax reform talks with the government that were seen by both sides as the last chance to achieve cross-party compromise.

Arriving for the negotiations, SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine said: "We are going into these talks with a will to agree. We want results...Any decision which serves the battle against unemployment will win our support."

Peter Hintze, general secretary of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), said the talks were a last bid for early compromise. If they fail, the government will seek to push Finance Minister Theo Waigel's package of 30 billion marks in tax cuts through the lower house of parliament by summer.
"The SPD must come clean today, and show whether it will stick to its blockade or participate in this great tax-cutting project to create more jobs in Germany," Hintze said.

The government wants to pass the tax reforms to give a boost to investment and reduce Germany's 4.5 million jobless. But the SPD can block most tax measures through its control of the upper house of parliament.
The talks were expected to last up to three hours.
